title: Unfinished algebraicity criterion for a mixed H¹ class
as_he_states: Scan89 ends with a request to prove that an unspecified class is algebraic; the condition and quantifiers are unfinished.
plausible_today: The normalized divisor/Hom correspondence is precise and classical; an arithmetic Tate statement requires a specified field and Galois invariance.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19. C-SA06-201: The divisor/Hom identification is classical Picard duality and the see-saw principle; Milne I §§8–9 supplies the construction. It gives no arbitrary-base Tate theorem: no Galois-invariance condition is supplied in the last sentence. That unfinished strengthening has no identifiable quantifier set.
why_open: No theorem can be matched to an omitted condition; lack of identification is not evidence of novelty.
worth: Worth a targeted ink/context reconstruction, not an attempted proof of an unspecified statement.

title: Finite freeness of numerical cycle classes
as_he_states: The numerical row of scan92 asks whether the group is free of finite type.
plausible_today: For smooth projective varieties with a Weil cohomology, the integral numerical quotient is finite free.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19. C-SA06-203: Kleiman1968 Thm3.5 proves finite freeness using a Weil cohomology. An independent proof chooses finitely many complementary algebraic classes spanning the cohomological algebraic subspace, and embeds the numerical group by integer intersection numbers into Z^r. Algebraic-equivalence quotients can have a nonzero, even infinite-dimensional Griffiths part.
why_open: The question has an established answer; the excerpt does not give its proof.
worth: Worth retaining as a precise historical match to Kleiman Theorem3.5, requiring no new research.

title: Finite differences between cycle equivalences
as_he_states: The chart asks Groupe fini? and marks maps between algebraic, homological, torsion and numerical relations with question marks.
plausible_today: State each equivalence relation and coefficient ring separately; numerical finite generation does not control the Griffiths quotient.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19. C-SA06-204: Numerical finite generation is C-SA06-203. Whole Chow or whole algebraically trivial cycle representability is false in general by Mumford1969; algebraic representatives exist in specific codimensions and are universal only for regular homomorphisms, as in Kahn2021 Thm0.1 for codimension2. The chart’s crossed integral/rational homology arrows are not a theorem. C-SA06-239: For a very general smooth quintic threefold over C and i=1, NS(X)_Q is finite-dimensional, while CH²(X)/alg tensored with Q contains an infinite-dimensional Griffiths group: Clemens1983 Thm0.2 plus Griffiths’s vanishing of the algebraic Abel–Jacobi image, stated there. Hence L cannot be surjective even rationally. The standard Lefschetz conjecture on cohomological algebraic classes remains a distinct question.
why_open: Clemens gives an infinite-dimensional rational obstruction to some proposed finite differences; the chart is not a single true theorem.
worth: Worth reconstructing each row individually and attaching known counterexamples.

title: Abelian representatives for continuous cycle quotients

state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19. C-SA06-204: Numerical finite generation is C-SA06-203. The chart’s crossed integral/rational homology arrows are not a theorem. title: Integral and rational cohomological rows of the chart

title: Removing the nonzero-section hypothesis in the ampleness argument
as_he_states: Scan95 asks whether the section hypothesis can be suppressed after the two lemmas.
plausible_today: The Euler-growth criterion holds under its proper/projective hypotheses; strict curve positivity alone does not imply ampleness.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19. C-SA06-218: This is the inductive mechanism in the cohomological ampleness criterion of Mumford–Oda VIII Thm1.11. The projectivity annotation is used to choose a hyperplane; replacing projective by arbitrary proper at this intermediate step requires a separate proof, though the final numerical criterion is known for proper X. C-SA06-219: The effective-divisor step is part of the Mumford–Oda ampleness proof. A nonzero section with empty divisor gives the trivial bundle, incompatible with positive restriction on a curve in a positive-dimensional projective X; a nonempty divisor enables induction. The manuscript asks whether the section hypothesis can be removed. C-SA06-220: It is false over C: Hartshorne1970,I Example10.6,p56, gives Mumford’s smooth projective ruled surface with a divisor D satisfying D.C>0 for every curve but D²=0. All proper positive-dimensional subvarieties are curves and D restricts amply to each, while D is not ample.
why_open: A strictly nef line bundle with square0 gives the obstruction to the naive section-free strengthening. The sources do not establish the author’s historical reason for abandoning it.
worth: Worth separating the exact induction hypotheses from the false strictly nef strengthening.

title: Strict positivity on curves versus ampleness
as_he_states: Scan96 asks whether strict positivity on every curve forces the class into the ample region; scan100 explores top intersections.
plausible_today: Strict nefness is weaker than ampleness, even with positive top self-intersection in dimension3.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19. C-SA06-220: It is false over C: Hartshorne1970,I Example10.6,p56, gives Mumford’s smooth projective ruled surface with a divisor D satisfying D.C>0 for every curve but D²=0. All proper positive-dimensional subvarieties are curves and D restricts amply to each, while D is not ample. C-SA06-221: Kleiman’s numerical criterion and Mumford’s counterexample distinguish these conditions. Hartshorne I Ex10.6,p56 checks the square-zero example; Mumford–Oda IX Thm1.15 gives the cone criterion. The draft’s strict-curve question is thus settled negatively, while the closed-cone equality holds. C-SA06-222: Independently construct X=P_S(O⊕A) over Mumford’s surface S, with A ample and L strictly nef with L²=0. For D=ξ+π*L, D is strictly nef, D³=A²+3A.L>0, but its square on the quotient section O is L²=0; hence it is not ample. Hartshorne I Ex10.8,pp57–58 gives Ramanujam’s related effective threefold counterexample.
why_open: Mumford’s surface and the checked projective-bundle threefold give concrete counterexamples; closed-cone boundary behavior is the obstruction.
worth: Worth developing only as a counterexample and hypothesis-classification exercise.

title: Euler-characteristic sign for an isotropic strict-nef divisor
as_he_states: Scan96 ends with an expected inequality for χ(D), with the sign itself uncertain.
plausible_today: On a smooth surface with D²=0, χ(nD)=χ(O)−nD·K/2; a sign needs an additional assertion about D·K and the intended n.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19. C-SA06-226: The calculation is exact. If D is strictly nef and not numerically trivial, no positive multiple can be represented by a nonzero effective divisor when D²=0. Together with eventual H²-vanishing this bounds the linear coefficient by0. Whether the written sign is < or≤ remains an ink question; the argument alone does not decide the glyph.
why_open: The uncertain operator and suppressed numerical hypotheses prevent a universal sign conclusion.
worth: Worth an ink check plus a Riemann–Roch type check, rather than a conjectural sign theorem.

title: Nef divisor powers and top intersection
as_he_states: Scan100 asks whether D·C≥0 for every curve implies nonnegative higher powers and D^d≥0, and uses a cubic expansion.
plausible_today: For projective varieties, nef divisor powers pair nonnegatively with effective cycles by approximation with ample divisors.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19. C-SA06-223: Approximate D by D+εH with H ample and pass to the limit in the finite-dimensional numerical cycle space. This elementary divisor argument does not extend to arbitrary higher-codimension nef classes. DELV2011 §1 reviews the distinction and TheoremA supplies counterexamples to that extension. C-SA06-227: The symbolic expansion is correct. It yields no general positivity theorem for products of higher-codimension nef cycles, which DELV2011 refutes.
why_open: This is established; the polynomial calculation alone was not the missing positivity input.

title: Products of nef higher-cycle classes
as_he_states: Scan100 asks for nonnegative pairings/products of the polar cones in complementary codimensions.
plausible_today: There is no universal product-closure theorem for arbitrary nef higher-codimension classes.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19. C-SA06-224: Debarre–Ein–Lazarsfeld–Voisin2011,TheoremA and Remark2.3, explicitly connect the question to Grothendieck’s31Aug1964letter and show on powers of a CM elliptic curve that nef higher-codimension classes can fail to be pseudoeffective and products of nef classes can fail to be nef. The precise numerical positivity cone is essential.

title: Irreducible-pencil control of Picard restriction
as_he_states: Scan103 presumes that irreducible limiting curves in suitable pencils force the indicated kernel behavior.
plausible_today: For a regular pencil with geometrically integral fibres, vertical divisors control generic restriction; a special-fibre injectivity theorem needs additional generality hypotheses.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19. C-SA06-228: Finite generation follows because its intersection with Pic⁰ is finite and its image in the finitely generated NS(X) is a subgroup. The numerical map need not have finite kernel: the page says finite cokernel and rankρ−1 kernel. The Picard/Albanese hyperplane comparison is classical and is compatible with SGA2 XII and Milne III §10. C-SA06-229: For a regular surface pencil with every fibre geometrically integral, a line bundle trivial on the generic fibre is vertical and, after imposing the base-point exceptional-section data, one can often force the original surface bundle to be trivial. This verifies the generic-fibre mechanism, not the stated special-fibre assertion for an arbitrary chosen Y. The MathOverflow233157 argument gives precise very-general hypersurface cases and points back to Lefschetz-pencil theory; no theorem with exactly the draft’s unquantified formulation was identified.
why_open: The draft does not specify the pencil quantifiers or specialization step. Starr’s precise very-general cases are narrower.
worth: Worth formulating and proving the generic-fibre statement first, then auditing specialization separately.

title: Local finite-generation and finite-error package
as_he_states: Scans106–107 conjecture local J,N,A finiteness in ranges and cite a Mumford–Hodge surface case.

state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19. C-SA06-230: The literal all-degree package is not a standard established theorem. Codimension1 local Lefschetz has precise modern results under additional normality, excellence, dimension and depth hypotheses (Bhatt–de Jong Thm0.1); complete-intersection local rings of dimension≥4 are parafactorial (Stacks0F2I). Neither source proves higher-Chow finiteness for arbitrary strictly local Noetherian A. The undefined local equivalence convention limits exact identification of N and J. C-SA06-234: Mumford1961 §1,p6 proves the intersection matrix is negative definite; its nonzero integral determinant gives a finite lattice cokernel. Identification with the particular locally defined N¹ on this sheet requires its omitted definition and the resolution hypotheses. The finite discriminant group must not be confused with the full local Picard group.
why_open: The local equivalence convention and N are not fully defined; surface discriminant lattices do not identify an arbitrary local Picard group.
worth: Worth reconstructing the local definitions and testing codimension1 before extending the package.

title: Local restriction and the critical index
as_he_states: Scan106 gives local restriction maps with finite-error and characteristic qualifications and singles out a critical case.

state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19. C-SA06-231: Bhatt–de Jong2014 Thm0.1 proves injectivity of local Picard restriction for excellent normal local A containing a field, dim A≥4; in characteristic0 it requires depth(A/f)≥2, while in characteristic p its kernel is p-power torsion. Their examples show the dimension/depth restrictions matter and surjectivity is not automatic. This is a restricted codimension1 realization, not the complete integral Chow package.
why_open: Higher codimensions and surjectivity are not consequences of that theorem; changing the singularity hypotheses changes the answer.
worth: Worth a theorem-by-theorem hypothesis comparison in codimension1.

title: Vanishing of local Gysin maps
as_he_states: Scan107 asks for vanishing of the local principal-divisor pushforward and treats the open-complement comparison as a consequence.

title: Global weak Lefschetz for rational-equivalence groups
as_he_states: Scan111 proposes restriction isomorphisms/injections in explicit codimension ranges, with exc.p? qualifications.
plausible_today: The rational Chow weak Lefschetz conjecture has the stated stable range i<dimY/2; Picard cases have classical theorems and infinitesimal K-cohomology has partial results.

Patel–Ravindra2014 Conj1.1 states it; Thm1.4 proves an infinitesimal K-cohomological result, not algebraization. In codimension1 classical Grothendieck–Lefschetz applies under its dimension/depth conditions. No universal integral finite-error theorem in the written range was found.

worth: Worth one focused run comparing a fixed codimension and class of varieties with the modern conjecture.

title: Global Gysin surjectivity on Chow groups
as_he_states: Scan111 gives a separate pushforward range from a smooth hyperplane Y to X.
plausible_today: The unrestricted Chow surjectivity is false already for CH0 of a K3 surface; quotients modulo algebraic equivalence have a different behavior.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19. C-SA06-238: At n=2,i=0, take a smooth projective complex K3 surface X and any smooth hyperplane curve Y. Surjectivity CH0(Y)_Q→CH0(X)_Q would make CH0(X) finite-dimensional in Mumford’s sense, contrary to H⁰(X,Ω²)≠0 and Mumford1969. The same obstruction applies to the surjectivity on the degree-zero/algebraically trivial part. The quotient modulo algebraic equivalence is a different, much smaller assertion.
why_open: Mumford’s theorem prevents a fixed curve from parameterizing all zero-cycles on a K3.
worth: Worth retaining the sharp K3 counterexample and reformulating only in a specified quotient.

title: Hard Lefschetz modulo algebraic equivalence
as_he_states: Scan112 asks for bijectivity modulo finite groups of the Lefschetz map on A_a.
plausible_today: On general smooth projective varieties this is false even rationally; on cohomological algebraic classes it becomes the distinct standard Lefschetz conjecture.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19. C-SA06-239: For a very general smooth quintic threefold over C and i=1, NS(X)_Q is finite-dimensional, while CH²(X)/alg tensored with Q contains an infinite-dimensional Griffiths group: Clemens1983 Thm0.2 plus Griffiths’s vanishing of the algebraic Abel–Jacobi image, stated there. Hence L cannot be surjective even rationally. The standard Lefschetz conjecture on cohomological algebraic classes remains a distinct question.
why_open: A very general quintic threefold has an infinite-dimensional Griffiths quotient, obstructing surjectivity from finite-rank divisor classes.
worth: Worth documenting the exact failure and avoiding substitution of numerical equivalence for the written a.

title: Lefschetz maps on algebraically trivial or τ subgroups
as_he_states: Scan112 revises the subgroup/quotient formulas and finite-error qualifications.
plausible_today: The unrestricted shifted surjectivity is false for a K3: Pic⁰ and Pic^τ vanish while CH0⁰ does not.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19. C-SA06-240: In the n=2,i=1 case, a complex K3 has Pic⁰=0 and nonzero CH0^0, so the analogous algebraically trivial map cannot be surjective. With τ interpreted as numerical or homological triviality up to torsion, Pic^τ of a K3 is also0, and the same obstruction applies. The explicit change of subscript on the page must be retained; no conjecture on a motivic associated-graded piece is written.
why_open: The proposed subgroup range does not track the extra Chow filtration needed by refined conjectures.
worth: Worth testing precise filtered replacements only after fixing the meaning of τ.

title: General powers on the whole Chow group
as_he_states: The last implication on scan112 proposes whole-Chow injectivity/surjectivity ranges.
plausible_today: No such universal surjectivity holds; refined Abel–Jacobi-trivial injectivity and Beauville-graded results are different statements.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19. C-SA06-241: For n=2,i=1,p=1 on a complex projective K3, Beauville–Voisin2004 Thm1 places all divisor products in Q·c_X, whereas Mumford1969 shows CH0(X)_Q is not finite-dimensional. Thus even the rational surjectivity fails. Laterveer2016 discusses refined injectivity on Abel–Jacobi-trivial cycles and proves conditional results, not this universal whole-Chow statement.
why_open: The K3 divisor-product image is one-dimensional while CH0 is not finite-dimensional.

title: Recovering an integral image from its top wedge
as_he_states: Scans83/85 ask whether determinant/top-wedge information determines the image and its degree.
plausible_today: The decomposable wedge determines the rational image subspace; determinant content does not determine the integral sublattice.
state_of_art: As of 2026-11-19. C-SA06-279: The first statement is the definition of proper cycle pushforward. The linear-algebra identity W={v:v∧ω=0} for a nonzero top wedgeω∈Λ^rW reconstructs W over a field; Milne Algebraic Groups Lem4.28 gives this exact identity. It determines a rational subspace, not an integral lattice. C-SA06-280: The sublatticesℓZℓe1+Zℓe2 andZℓe1+ℓZℓe2 are different but have the same determinant lineℓZℓ(e1∧e2). They also have the same rational span. Thus the page’s rational recovery of the image subspace is valid, while the stronger integral reading is not.
why_open: Two explicit diagonal lattices have the same determinant line and different images.
worth: Worth distinguishing rational span, lattice index and lattice position in the intended claim.
